Title: Phonetic enhancement of Mandarin vowels and tones: Infant-directed speech and Lombard speech.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 15 Mandarin-speaking mothers interacting with their 12-month-old infants
Stimulus_Type: eight-talker babble noise environment (Lombard speech condition); infant-directed speech
Outcome: Vowel space expansion in IDS and Lombard speech; tone space expansion only in IDS utterance-final position
Evidence_Quote: Vowel and tone productions were produced by 15 Mandarin-speaking mothers during interactions with their 12-month-old infants during a play session (IDS), in conversation with a Mandarin-speaking adult in a 70 dBA eight-talker babble noise environment (Lombard speech), and in a quiet environment (adult-directed speech).

Title: Acoustic parameters of infant-directed singing in mothers of infants with down syndrome.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Target_Age: infants between 3 and 9 months of age
Outcome: acoustic parameters; perceived warmth
Evidence_Quote: This study compared the acoustic parameters and degree of perceived warmth in two types of infant-directed (ID) songs - the lullaby and the playsong

Title: Rhythmic ostensive gestures: How adults facilitate infants' entrance into early triadic interactions.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Outcome: child responses; understanding of communicative intention
Evidence_Quote: We conducted a longitudinal study with 6 babies filmed at 2, 3 and 4 months old in interaction with their mothers and a sounding object (a maraca).

Title: A fully automated approach for baby cry signal segmentation and boundary detection of expiratory and inspiratory episodes.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: cry signal segmentation; expiratory and inspiratory episode detection
Evidence_Quote: This full approach allows to precisely determine the start and end points of the expiratory and inspiratory components of a cry signal, EXP and INSV, respectively, in any given sound signal.

Title: Acoustic realization of Mandarin neutral tone and tone sandhi in infant-directed speech and Lombard speech.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: acoustic realization of neutral tone and tone sandhi; pitch height; pitch contour
Evidence_Quote: Neutral tone and tone sandhi productions were elicited from 15 Mandarin-speaking mothers during (1) interactions with their 12-month-old infants (IDS), (2) in conversation with a Mandarin-speaking adult in a noisy environment (Lombard speech), and (3) in conversation with a Mandarin-speaking adult in a quiet environment (adult-directed speech).

Title: Heart rate variability in neonates of type 1 diabetic pregnancy.
Journal: Early human development
Outcome: heart rate variability
Evidence_Quote: Heart rate variability assessment and cord blood sampling for pH and glucose were performed for all neonates.

Title: Longitudinal development of wideband reflectance tympanometry in normal and at-risk infants.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: infants followed longitudinally from birth to one year of age
Stimulus_Type: wideband middle ear acoustic test battery; tympanometry
Outcome: wideband acoustic reflectance; absorbance; group delay
Evidence_Quote: They were tested longitudinally for up to one year using a wideband middle ear acoustic test battery consisting of tympanometry and ambient-pressure tests.

Title: Impact of maternal physical activity on fetal breathing and body movement--A review.
Journal: Early human development
Outcome: fetal body movement; fetal breathing movement
Evidence_Quote: This paper will provide a brief review of the literature and outline the current knowledge with regards to the effects of maternal exercise on fetal body and breathing movements.

Title: Heterogeneity of vocal sac inflation patterns in Odorrana tormota plays a role in call diversity.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: recorded male calls (audio/video); no presented stimulus
Outcome: Short calls with F0 >5000 Hz inflated pars lateralis only; calls with F0 <4000 Hz inflated pars ventralis only
Evidence_Quote: Short call-types (duration <200 ms) involved inflation of one of the compartments only; those having a fundamental frequency (F0) of >5000 Hz involved inflation of pars lateralis only, whereas those with an F0 of <4000 Hz (tone-pips and "infant" calls) involved inflation of pars ventralis only.

Title: Speech rate and pitch characteristics of infant-directed speech: Longitudinal and cross-linguistic observations.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants beginning when the infant was 4 months old
Outcome: speech rate; pitch (F0) characteristics
Evidence_Quote: The speech rate and pitch (F0) characteristics of naturalistic, longitudinally recorded infant- and adult-directed speech are reported for three, genetically diverse languages.

Title: Subcortical neural representation to Mandarin pitch contours in American and Chinese newborns.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: ten American and ten Chinese newborns
Outcome: frequency-following responses; tracking accuracy; response amplitudes
Evidence_Quote: This study examines the neural representation of voice pitch at the subcortical level, as reflected by the scalp-recorded frequency-following responses from ten American and ten Chinese newborns.

Title: Seasonal variations in auditory processing in the inferior colliculus of Eptesicus fuscus.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: responses of single neurons in the inferior colliculus
Evidence_Quote: To explore the possibility that seasonal changes in hormonal status could drive functional plasticity in the central auditory system, we examined responses of single neurons in the inferior colliculus throughout the year.

Title: Learnability of prosodic boundaries: Is infant-directed speech easier?
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: prosodic boundary classification
Evidence_Quote: Statistical analyses run on a large database of mother-child and mother-interviewer interactions showed that the duration of a pause and the duration of the syllable nucleus preceding the boundary are two cues which are enhanced in IDS, while f0 change is actually degraded in IDS.

Title: Infant-directed speech reduces English-learning infants' preference for trochaic words.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: listening preference for trochaic words
Evidence_Quote: To address this question, 9-month-old American infants were familiarized and tested with both trochaic (e.g., lazy) and iambic (e.g., cartoon) words presented in either IDS or adult-directed speech (ADS).

Title: Stimulus-frequency otoacoustic emissions in human newborns.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Neonates had adult-like SFOAE delays when compared at linear-growth stimulus levels
Evidence_Quote: SFOAEs in newborns were measured at stimulus levels as low as 15 dB sound pressure level (SPL). Responses were compared between adults and newborns at stimulus levels where SFOAEs in both age groups demonstrated approximately linear growth (<40 dB SPL for newborns, <25 dB SPL for adults).

Title: Intersensory redundancy promotes visual rhythm discrimination in visually impaired infants.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Outcome: visual rhythm discrimination; attention
Evidence_Quote: Evidence from this study demonstrates that intersensory redundancy can facilitate discrimination of rhythm changes presented in the visual modality alone in visually impaired infants, suggesting that multisensory rehabilitation strategies could prove helpful in this population.

Title: Self-Regulation and Infant-Directed Singing in Infants with Down Syndrome.
Journal: Journal of music therapy
Outcome: infant gaze; affect; self-regulation
Evidence_Quote: The researcher explored responses to ID singing in infants with Down syndrome (DS) and compared them with those of typically developing (TD) infants. Behaviors measured included infant gaze and affect as indicators of self-regulation.

Title: Development of subcortical speech representation in human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 28 infants, ages three to ten months
Outcome: frequency following response
Evidence_Quote: Here, FFRs were recorded to a speech syllable in 28 infants, ages three to ten months.

Title: Frequency-change in DPOAE evoked by 1 s/octave sweeping primaries in newborns and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: distortion product otoacoustic emissions
Evidence_Quote: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAE) in newborns and adults were evoked by sweeping primaries up and down in frequency at 1 s/octave.

Title: Modified spectral tilt affects infants' native-language discrimination of approximants and vowels.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds /r/-/l/ and /ɔ/-/ɐ/ with modified spectral tilt (-6 / +6 dB/octave)
Outcome: 6-month-olds discriminated in spectrally modified conditions; 9-month-olds only when unmodified
Evidence_Quote: Infants were presented with /r/-/l/ and /ɔ/-/ɐ/ in three conditions: (a) unmodified; (b) -6 dB/octave tilt; and (c) +6 dB/octave tilt.

Title: The role of prosody in infants' early syntactic analysis and grammatical categorization.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: word categorization; syntactic interpretation
Evidence_Quote: Infants perceived the test-stimuli according to the familiarized structure. They used prosody to categorize words and interpret adjacent and non-adjacent syntactic dependencies.
